doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

title: Borough-wide band, orchestra and Music and Art High School
summary: Progress on tuba through the Manhattan band and orchestra into Music and Art High School with a tubist mentor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You were like one on a part, too.

Yeah. Definitely one on a part. So I moved into the orchestra setting at the junior high school level. And then I carried that up. And when I graduated from junior high school I went to a very very prestigious high school in New York called Music and Art High School. Music and Art High School is known because of the sister school called Performing Arts. That movie “Fame” was based on Performing Arts. But Music and Art and Performing Arts were like sister schools or brother schools, depending on your perspective. So I was surrounded at that particular point, you know, with these very very creative young people and very creative and talented musicians and everything. And my tuba playing at that particular time, you know, got really profound. Because you know I had a couple of mentors when I entered Music and Art, one of them already was in the

All-City High School Orchestra, which was the most prestigious orchestra in New York at that time for high school students. So he was like the tubist in that orchestra. So I just followed him around. And every time he practiced I’d practice and then I became very very proficient.
